label: #3619127: sidebar opens from Inline Form Errors links (MR + vanilla JS), pinned core
description: Before: upstream main. After: MR !16895 with patch-0 (no jQuery) and patch-1 (no persist). Open /node/add/article in a narrow window, set a URL alias of 'no-slash' inside the sidebar, close the sidebar, Save, then use the error link. Before: nothing opens. After: the sidebar opens and the field gets focus.

steps.text: Default Admin is the admin theme.
Article content type and the Path module (URL alias field) are installed.
The Inline Form Errors module is enabled.
Open /node/add/article (the page is already loaded in both frames once you press Go).
Use the Tablet or Phone frame width, so the sidebar of advanced fields is collapsed.
Click "Expand sidebar" to open it.
Open "URL alias" and type a value without a leading slash, for example no-slash.
Close the sidebar.
Click Save. An error appears at the top: "1 error has been found: URL alias", with "URL alias" as a link.
steps.lookFor: An error summary at the top of the page, with "URL alias" as a link. If you do not see it, the setup went wrong; try again from step 6.

steps.text: Turn Mirror off. In EACH frame, click the "URL alias" link with a REAL mouse click (then repeat using only the keyboard: Tab to the link, press Enter). Do not use a script: script-generated clicks do not trigger the focus behaviour being tested.
steps.lookFor: Before: nothing visibly happens. After: the sidebar opens and the URL alias box is outlined (it has keyboard focus). Then press Run checks.

expected: The sidebar opens and keyboard focus moves to the invalid URL alias field.
actual: Before (upstream main): nothing happens. After (with the change): the sidebar opens and the field has focus.
setup: scripts/lab-site.sh reset <env> (or apply <env>) gives a site in the starting state for steps 1 to 3.

checks.label: Setup reached: error link to URL alias is on the page
The error link was used with a real click or key press, not a script
Sidebar is open after using the error link
URL alias field received keyboard focus (recorded when it happens: only one frame can hold focus at a time)
Saved sidebar preference was not overwritten (phone/tablet key)
JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless "ResizeObserver loop" notice)
Number of open details sections matches the other side

observe.label: The sidebar of advanced fields opened by itself
The "URL alias" section is open and the field is visible without scrolling
The "URL alias" field has a visible focus outline
Anything else looks broken or different (layout, colours, errors)

label: #3604037: groups (details, vertical tabs) that contain a field error say so, pinned core
description: Forms group fields in closed <details> and vertical tabs. When a field inside a closed or inactive group has an error, nothing on the group says so. The change (MR !17078, Default Admin theme) marks such groups with a red border, an icon, red label text, a hidden " (contains error)" label for screen readers and a data-child-error-count attribute. Follow the steps on three pages, then press Run checks on each page: the checks apply to the page the frames are on. Both sites carry the same test-page change (a second required field), so the page looks the same on both sides; only the code under test differs.
status: stub: fill in pages, steps, expected, checks, observe

steps.text: Default Admin is the admin theme.

Type /form_test/details-contains-required-fields in Page and press Go (both). A form appears with a collapsible section that contains required fields.
steps.lookFor: A details section titled something like "Meta" with two required text fields inside.

steps.text: Press the form's submit button without filling in anything.
steps.lookFor: Error messages for the required fields.

steps.text: Close the details section by clicking its title.
steps.lookFor: Before: a plain closed section, nothing says it contains errors. After: it is marked as containing errors (red border, error icon, red title). Then press Run checks.

steps.text: Open /node/add/article. Open the sidebar, open "URL alias", type a value with no leading slash (no-slash), close the sidebar, press Save.
steps.lookFor: Open the sidebar again: After marks the "URL alias" group as containing an error even though it is closed. Run checks.

steps.lookFor: The tab that contains the error is marked in After but not in Before. Run checks.

steps.text: Forced colours: press Open forced-colours window in the viewer, then in the new window press Log in both as admin, choose Forced colours, light (and later dark) and repeat step 5 and step 7. (docs/FORCED-COLORS.md has other ways.)

steps.lookFor: The same red bar and icon appear on the section with the error, and the bar is not covered when the section is focused.

steps.lookFor: The server-rendered error markers still appear on After (class error and a data-child-error-count attribute); there are none on Before.

actual: Before the change a closed or inactive group gives no sign that a field inside it has an error; the user must open each group to find it.

#3093378: ARIA disclosure for vertical toolbar submenu buttons (contrib toolbar 2.x, current core main)
description: The toolbar module has moved out of Drupal core into the contrib project 'toolbar'. Both sites run current core main with contrib toolbar 2.x at commit 871ce78 checked out into modules/contrib/toolbar and enabled. Before: the module as-is. After: the module with merge request !6 applied (a real ARIA disclosure: aria-expanded plus a '<name> menu' accessible name, and no text-indent hack). The change is meant to be visually identical, so the difference is in the markup and the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

steps.text: Standard install on current core main with the contrib toolbar module (2.x, commit 871ce78) in modules/contrib and enabled. Default Admin is the admin theme.
Open the home page. The administration toolbar runs across the top of the page.
Open the 'Manage' tray (click the Manage tab in the toolbar).
steps.lookFor: A bar of administration menu links: Content, Structure, Appearance, Extend, Configuration, People, Reports.

steps.text: Expand a section that has a submenu by clicking its disclosure button (the chevron next to 'Structure').
steps.lookFor: The submenu opens. Visually nothing about the button changes: an icon, no visible text.

steps.text: In EACH frame, inspect the disclosure button's markup and accessibility (or press Run checks). Before: a hidden span flips between 'Extend' and 'Collapse' and there is no aria-expanded. After: aria-expanded is 'false' then 'true' and the hidden name is 'Structure menu'.
steps.lookFor: Before the name of the button is the opposite of its state (a toggle label); After the state is separate (aria-expanded) and the name stays 'Structure menu'.

expected: The disclosure button reports its state with aria-expanded and its accessible name is the submenu's link text followed by ' menu' (for example 'Structure menu'). No visual change.
actual: Before, the same button carries no aria-expanded and its name flips between 'Extend' and 'Collapse', conflating the name with the state.

checks.label: Setup reached: the toolbar renders disclosure buttons
A disclosure button carries aria-expanded (the machine-readable state)
The toggle button's label ends with ' menu' (not 'Extend'/'Collapse')
The old 'Extend'/'Collapse' action span is gone
JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless "ResizeObserver loop" notice)
The same number of disclosure buttons is rendered on both sides

observe.label: The toolbar and its submenu buttons look the same as before the change (same icon, no visible text)
Clicking the disclosure button opens and closes the submenu
The button's state is exposed to assistive tech as aria-expanded
Anything else looks broken, overlapped or different (layout, colours, spacing)

#3619154: Sidebar toggle fixes, pinned core
description: MR !16911 at 175e6f17 (2026-10-17; the lab reviewed 6f7766cb on 2026-10-14) reworks the Default Admin node add/edit meta sidebar: sidebar.js is split into a sidebar-toggle SDC + edit-sidebar.js; the toggle and close controls become <button> elements with aria-expanded; below 1024px the content under the overlay is inert, focus moves to the close button and Escape closes it; the sidebar sits below the top bar and does not flash on load; the resize handle works after AJAX, with touch and in RTL. Test on /node/1/edit across widths. Scripted: tools/playwright/evaluate-3619154.mjs (steps and checks in tools/playwright/sidebar-3619154.mjs).
status: ready: MR !16911 at 175e6f17 on core main f2abd41 (re-pinned 2026-10-18 from 6868135a, where the new patch's Umami performance-test hunk no longer applies). The 2026-10-14 review of 6f7766cb is in original-patches/ and its run is now stale.

steps.text: Default Admin is the admin theme.
Article content type, the Navigation module and one article node are installed.
Open /node/1/edit (loaded in both frames once you press Go).
Focus the sidebar toggle (top of the meta sidebar) and press the Space key.
steps.lookFor: After: the sidebar toggles. Before: nothing happens — an <a role=button> does not activate on Space.

steps.text: Desktop (>=1024px): toggle the sidebar closed, then reload the frame.
steps.lookFor: Neither side should show the open sidebar while the page loads, and it stays closed. Measured 2026-10-17: no flash on either side at 1280px; Before's flash is on a first visit below 1024px (next step).

steps.text: Below 1024px, with no stored sidebar state (first visit, or clear Drupal.defaultAdmin.* in localStorage), load /node/1/edit.
steps.lookFor: After: the sidebar never appears during the load. Before: it is painted on screen for a few frames, then hidden.

steps.text: Toggle the sidebar open, drag the resize handle, then reload.
steps.lookFor: After: open state and the chosen width persist after reload.

steps.text: At 1100px, with the sidebar open and Navigation expanded, open and close a details element in the main column (Image).
steps.lookFor: After: Navigation stays expanded. Below 1280px a click that opens one panel closes the other on both sides, so both are open only after a reload from stored state; on Before that reload collapses Navigation.

steps.text: Narrow the frame below 1024px and open the sidebar.
steps.lookFor: After: focus moves to the close button; Tab stays within the sidebar, Navigation and the top bar (the page behind is inert); Escape closes it and returns focus to the toggle; the sidebar starts below the top bar. Before: the sidebar's top (and its close button) is under the top bar, focus stays on the toggle and Tab reaches the covered page. The resize handle is hidden below 976px.

steps.text: Forced colours (local DDEV: the lab browser's switch; any lab: DevTools > Rendering > Emulate forced-colors, or a Windows contrast theme), below 976px: open the sidebar with Enter.
steps.lookFor: After: the close button has focus and its × icon is visible inside the focus ring. With revision 6f7766cb only the ring showed (comment #23); with 175e6f17 the icon shows (measured 2026-10-18, Chromium). Before: the close button is under the top bar.

steps.text: Below 976px: close the sidebar once with the close button and once by clicking the overlay.
steps.lookFor: The sidebar closes and the URL does not change.

steps.text: Desktop: set dir="rtl" on <html> (DevTools), then drag the resize handle outward (towards the middle of the page).
steps.lookFor: After: the sidebar gets wider. Before: it gets narrower.

expected: After: the toggle and close are <button> elements operable with Enter and Space; aria-expanded tracks the sidebar state; open/closed state and width persist across reloads; nothing is painted on load below 1024px; below 1024px the content under the overlay is inert, focus moves to the close button, Escape closes the sidebar and returns focus to the toggle, and the sidebar starts below the top bar. Before: <a href="#" role="button"> controls, Space does not operate them, no inert overlay or focus trap, and the sidebar starts under the top bar below 1024px.
actual: MR !16911 at 175e6f17 on core main f2abd41, scratch run 2026-10-18 (not DDEV): reproduced-and-fixed in normal and forced colours (11 of 12 fix checks as expected, F11 not applicable on Before; 14 regression checks pass; 0 axe violations). R12, the close button's icon with focus in forced colours (comment #23), now passes: 76 icon pixels focused, 64 at rest (12 with 6f7766cb). reports/issues/3619154/validation/2026-10-18-scratch-175e6f17/SUMMARY.md
